notes: Real bug, exact mechanism (read from the diff, not the PR title): _tempfilepager writes a temp file, closes it, then runs the pager, with `os.unlink(f.name)` in a finally. If anything raises before that explicit close(), the finally unlinks a still-open handle; on Windows that raises PermissionError, which REPLACES the original exception rather than letting it surface. The fix adds an idempotent f.close() in the finally before the unlink. So the defect is a cleanup path masking the real error, with an unclosed handle as the root cause -- not simply 'an error was swallowed'. Getting this description right matters because a reconstruction is built from it. Confidence 0.75 rather than 0.8+: 72 lines across a changelog file plus source+test, and a platform-conditional failure is harder to isolate cleanly than a pure logic bug. NOTE: this is a merge commit; parent_commit above is its first parent, which is the diff GitHub and `git diff <parent> <commit>` both show. Recommend 'transformed', not 'verbatim': rebuild a minimal write-temp-file-then-hand-off-then-unlink wrapper with the same masking behaviour rather than copying click's pager implementation. Category fit: error-handling (an exception in cleanup masking the original) -- v2 has 4 error-handling cases, none about cleanup-path masking.
